text.p: Alliance Pharmaceutical Corp said Monday it temporarily suspended enrollment in its Phase III LiquiVent pediatric clinical trial due to an unexplained and substantial decrease in the mortality rate of the control group.

The trial, which was testing LiquiVent as a treatment for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), began in January of 1996 and had enrolled close to 200 patients. The trial had been designed so that mortality was the primary endpoint. Historically, the mortality rate in pediatric patients with ARDS is more than 30 percent, Alliance said.
However, in the Alliance trial, the mortality rate dropped to a percentage the company did not specify, but said was in the single-digit range.

The company also did not disclose the mortality rate in the test group, although a spokeswoman said it was less than the 30 percent historical mortality rate of patients with ARDS and was not a factor in the decision to suspend the trials.

Liquivent is a liquid form of oxygen that is suffused into the patient's lungs as a way to avoid lengthy periods on ventilators that are associated with several health problems and in some cases, death.
